answers.docs.gaps:
1. Wrong: docs/topics/app-configuration.md, "Static Context":

       App::builder()
           .context("version", "1.0.0")
           .context("app_name", "MyApp")

   `context` takes `minijinja::value::Value`, so both lines fail to compile
   without `.into()`. The dynamic-context example immediately below is correct
   because it constructs a `Value` explicitly.

2. Missing: the `\[` / `\]` escape is documented only under help text
   (docs/topics/standout-help.md), never in
   docs/crates/render/topics/templating.md or
   docs/crates/render/topics/styling-system.md, which are where a template
   author looks. Since the styling section of styling-system.md warns that an
   unknown tag gets a `?` marker in `Term`, any application that prints
   bracketed data needs this and has no way to find it from the templating
   pages.

3. Inconsistent: docs/crates/dispatch/topics/handler-contract.md declares
   `pub app_state: Rc<Extensions>` (line ~488) but the test example lower on
   the same page builds a context with `app_state: Arc::new(app_state)`
   (line ~705). One of the two is stale.

4. Missing: nothing documents how a template reaches data that must stay out of
   the serialized payload. docs/topics/app-configuration.md says dynamic
   context providers "receive `RenderContext` with output mode, terminal width,
   and handler data" but names no accessor for that handler data, so
   `context_fn` could not be used with any confidence; static `.context(...)`
   computed before `App::build()` was the only reachable option.

5. Missing: `--output` rejects a second occurrence, which matters to any
   application that wants to preselect an output mode. Neither
   docs/topics/output-modes.md nor docs/topics/app-configuration.md's "Flag
   Customization" section mentions it, and neither offers a builder-level
   default output mode.

6. Missing: `ExternalFailure`'s contract in docs/topics/error-handling.md states
   only that "Construction rejects status `0`". Whether an empty diagnostic is
   accepted is unstated; it is, and that is what makes an exit status with no
   output expressible.
answers.friction:
1. The documented `.context(...)` call does not compile. docs/topics/app-configuration.md
   shows `.context("version", "1.0.0")` and `.context("app_name", "MyApp")`.
   That produced:

       error[E0308]: mismatched types
          --> src/main.rs:145:33
           |
       145 |         .context("show_origin", show_origin)
           |          -------                ^^^^^^^^^^^ expected `Value`, found `&str`
       help: call `Into::into` on this expression to convert `&'static str` into `minijinja::value::Value`

   The fix is a trailing `.into()`, which the third example on that page
   (`.context("version", env!("CARGO_PKG_VERSION").into())`) happens to have
   and the first two do not.

2. Steering the framework's own output mode from the config layer. `term.output`
   has to reach the framework, and the only documented seam is the `--output`
   flag, so `main` resolves the configuration first and rewrites the argument
   vector. Appending the resolved mode was not enough:

       $ cargolike metadata --output json
       error: the argument '--output <MODE>' cannot be used multiple times

   so the program now strips any `--output` the line carries before appending
   its own. Nothing in the docs suggests an alternative (an `AppBuilder` knob
   that sets the default output mode would remove the rewrite entirely).

3. `config list`'s JSON shape and its human shape cannot both come from the
   handler's data. SPEC.md pins the JSON to "one object mapping each key to its
   value", so the top-level template variables are named `build.jobs`,
   `term.color`, and so on — names a MiniJinja template cannot iterate or even
   address, since `{{ build.jobs }}` is attribute access on `build`. The same
   payload has no room for `--show-origin`'s origins. docs/topics/output-modes.md
   is explicit that this is by design ("A handler should return the same
   serializable data regardless of whether the caller selected terminal, text,
   or structured output"), so the rendered lines are injected as template
   context instead. See the workarounds answer.

4. Literal `[` in output. `build`'s `features=[]` and `config list`'s
   `build.features = []` sit inside text that pass 2 reads as style tags, and
   docs/crates/render/topics/templating.md says nothing about emitting a
   literal bracket. The escape is documented one page away, for help text only
   (docs/topics/standout-help.md line 200: "To emit a literal `[` or `]` in
   help text, escape it with a backslash: `\[` and `\]`"). It does work in
   ordinary templates; I confirmed by running the binary.

5. The trailing-newline contract in docs/crates/render/topics/templating.md is
   precise about the template's *final* newline but says nothing about the
   engine's block-trimming settings, so a natural `{% for %}` … `\n` …
   `{% endfor %}` template could produce a trailing blank line or none
   depending on `trim_blocks`. Rather than depend on an unstated setting, every
   template here is a single line that emits separators as `{{ "\n" }}`.

answers.summary:
`cargolike` is complete and behaves as SPEC.md describes; `cargo build` is clean
(the only warning is sandbox `xcrun` noise from the linker probe, not from the
crate).

Layout in `app/src/`:

- `workspace.rs` — the frozen three-package workspace and the `-p` selection.
- `config.rs` — the known keys, `Value`/`Kind` types, text and TOML readers,
  the layer loaders (user file, walk-up project files, environment, `--config`,
  flags), and the per-type merge: scalars take the highest layer whole, lists
  concatenate across file layers (user items first, then farthest ancestor
  through nearest) and are *replaced* rather than appended by the environment
  or `--config`, with `--features` appending on top. Origins are tracked per
  key, collapsing to `merged` when a list drew items from more than one layer.
- `state.rs` — the resolved configuration as app state, plus the mapping from
  the app's own errors to exit statuses.
- `handlers.rs` — the five handlers (`metadata`, `tree`, `build`,
  `config get`, `config list`), each returning serializable view data.
- `views.rs` — the view structs, shaped so the JSON mode emits exactly the
  objects the spec pins.
- `main.rs` — the clap surface, the `Dispatch` enums, and the wiring.
- `templates/` and `styles/default.css`.

Verified by running the binary: the exact bytes of `metadata`, `tree`, `build`,
`config get` and `config list` (including trailing-newline behavior via
`xxd`); every exit code (0, 1 with both streams empty, 2 for unknown
commands/flags/config keys and `--config` without `=`, 101 for invalid values,
`build.jobs` below 1, unknown file keys and unknown packages); all four error
prose lines; the full precedence ladder
(flag > `--config` > env > `NO_COLOR` > nearer project file > farther project
file > user file > default) with real config files at two directory levels plus
a user file reached both through `CARGOLIKE_CONFIG_HOME` and through
`$HOME/.config/cargolike`; list concatenation, environment replacement,
environment clearing, and `--features` appending; every `--show-origin` value
including `merged`; and the JSON mode for all five commands. Styling was
checked with `CARGOLIKE_TERM_COLOR=always` (ANSI present) against the plain
bytes with color off.
answers.workarounds:
1. `main` builds the app twice and parses twice. The resolved configuration has
   to exist before `App::build()` (it supplies both the app state and the
   template context), but resolving it needs `--config`, `--jobs` and
   `--features` off the parsed line. So a throwaway app parses with
   `get_matches_from`, the configuration resolves, and the real app is built.
   `app/src/main.rs`, `fn main`.

2. The framework's `--output` is read off the raw argv rather than out of the
   parse (`typed_output`), because the flag carries a clap default and the
   parse cannot distinguish "the user typed `auto`" from "nobody typed
   anything" — and that distinction is exactly what makes `--output` the flag
   layer for `term.output`. The resolved mode is then written back by stripping
   and re-appending the flag (`without_output`).

3. `config get` and `config list` render their human lines in `main`
   (`config_views`) and pass them in through `.context(...)`, because their
   serialized payloads are pinned by the spec and have no room for either the
   origins or an iterable shape. The templates are one interpolation each. If
   the framework grew a way to hand the template data that structured output
   skips, this would collapse into two ordinary templates.

4. `serde_json`'s `preserve_order` feature is enabled in `Cargo.toml` so that
   JSON objects come out in the field order SPEC.md's examples show
   (`name`, `version`, `dependencies`) rather than alphabetically. This works
   by Cargo's feature unification reaching the `serde_json` the framework
   itself serializes with — it is a real dependency on that unification, not a
   local setting.

5. Every template is written as a single line whose loops emit `{{ "\n" }}`
   separators, so the output bytes do not depend on the engine's block-trimming
   configuration, which the docs do not state.

6. `ExternalFailure` carries all of the app's own exit statuses (1, 2 and 101)
   and its diagnostic prose. docs/topics/error-handling.md frames it as being
   for "an authoritative external failure … such as a delegated Git
   invocation", so this stretches the intent — but it is the only documented
   way an application can own an exit status other than 0, 1 and 2, and it is
   also what keeps handlers from printing or calling `process::exit`.
